cells.tense: You are holding two needs at once, right now, and keeping both alive.
cells.place: the pattern beneath the particulars — the shape of it, stripped of the story
cells.ask: offer one thing you've been carrying to the recognition that would let it be finished — an ending taken as arrival, not loss.
cells.core:
You can feel the shape of what's actually needed here, under everything that's being said about it. Two demands are pulling at you and you haven't dropped either one — you're tending both, deciding what each one gets and when, and neither of them is starving for it. That's the work. It doesn't need a name from you, it just keeps running.

What you're tending is growing because you're not forcing it. You're giving what's needed when it's needed, no more, and the thing is steady under that. There's care in it, and there's a clear eye in it, and the two aren't fighting each other.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending both demands, and neither one is starving for it.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead there's a version of this where everything you're tending comes through, and you're living there already.
cells.place: the pattern beneath the particulars — the shape of it, stripped of the story
cells.ask: put the picture down for one day and look at what's actually here — vision that comes from having lived something through, not from the shape it might take.
cells.core:
You're managing the future of everything you care for, and you're managing it hard. Each thing you tend, you already have the harvest mapped — what it should become, when it should get there, what it means if it doesn't. The care is real. The grip is also real, and the grip runs on a story that hasn't happened yet.

There's a plan in your hands that no one asked you to hold this tightly. The stewarding is turning into steering, and steering that far ahead of what's here stops being care. Things don't grow faster for being wanted that way.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending the harvest instead of what's actually in front of you.

cells.tense: There was a moment back there when tending something meant it could be taken, and you're still standing behind it.
cells.place: the pattern beneath the particulars — the shape of it, stripped of the story
cells.ask: stay with one small thing you've been quietly sticking with — resilience comes from the cultivation itself, and radiance from what's been carried to completion.
cells.core:
You know how to tend things. That hasn't gone anywhere. What's gone is the showing of it — somewhere back there, the caring got you something you didn't expect, so you stopped putting it where it could be seen. The pattern is still there in you. You read it fine. You've just stopped acting like it's yours to work with.

So the care has gone underground. It still runs — you notice what needs tending — but it doesn't reach all the way to your hands anymore. What's missing isn't the capacity. It's the willingness to keep going at it in the open.
cells.sheetLine: You still see what needs tending. You've just stopped reaching for it.

cells.tense: You're already doing it — deciding what stays and what goes, what gets fed and what gets let alone — and you call it something else.
cells.place: the pattern beneath the particulars — the shape of it, stripped of the story
cells.ask: name one thing you've been tending as yours — not the situation's, not the group's — and let someone see the shaping that's actually coming from you.
cells.core:
The steering is happening and you're the one at the wheel. You decide what gets time, what gets resources, what's worth holding, what gets set down. That capability is running all day. But you talk about it like you're just responding to what's needed — like the shape of things is arriving on its own and you're only reacting to it.

Under all the practicality there's a decision-maker who hasn't put their name on the decisions. What you've built has your shape in it. You can feel that about others' work without seeing it about your own.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping what's around you. You just haven't put your name on it.
